blocks.content: 1.1 Definition, Scope and Evolution of HRM

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Human Resource Management (HRM) is a strategic, proactive approach focused on nurturing human capital and aligning people management with organizational goals.
Personnel Management is traditional, administrative, and rule-bound, whereas HRM treats employees as valuable organizational assets and strategic partners.
HRM functions are split into Managerial Functions (Planning, Organizing, Directing, Controlling) and Operative Functions (Procurement, Development, Compensation, Maintenance, Integration).
HR Planning (Manpower Planning) systematically forecasts future demand and supply of human capital to eliminate skill surpluses or shortages.
Demand forecasting uses quantitative techniques (Trend Analysis, Ratio Analysis, Workload/Workforce Analysis) and qualitative techniques (Delphi Method, Expert Judgment).

blocks.content: Human Resource Management (HRM) is the strategic and coherent approach to managing an organisation's most valued assets :the people who work there :so that they individually and collectively contribute to the achievement of its objectives. HRM encompasses all activities related to acquiring, developing, motivating, and retaining employees.

blocks.content: HR Planning is the process by which an organisation ensures that it has the right number of people, with the right skills, in the right place, at the right time. It bridges the gap between present HR inventory and future HR requirements.

items: Delphi Technique is a qualitative forecasting method using an anonymous panel of experts to reach a consensus across multiple rounds.
Workload Analysis calculates required human resources from expected output, while Workforce Analysis measures current availability considering absenteeism and turnover.
Questions frequently distinguish Personnel Management (cost/tool oriented) from HRM (asset/strategic oriented).
Step 1 :Analyse Organisational Plans: Business objectives, expansion plans, automation decisions
Step 2 :Current HR Inventory: Skills audit, organisational chart, job analysis, role assessment
Step 3 :Demand Forecasting: Techniques :Managerial judgement, Regression analysis, Ratio-trend analysis, Work-study technique, Delphi method
Step 4 :Supply Forecasting: Internal (promotions, transfers, returns from leave) + External (labour market, universities, immigration)
Step 5 :Gap Analysis: Surplus (retrenchment, VRS, transfers) or Deficit (recruitment, outsourcing, overtime, automation)
Step 6 :Action Plans: Recruit, train, transfer, retire, redeploy, restructure
Step 7 :Monitoring and Control: Budgets, reports, HR audits
